item.description:

item.title: Fixing Eclipse Errors When Running with Java 9 Modules
item.description:
“Fixing Eclipse Errors When Running with Java 9 Modules”

Configuring Eclipse for Java 9 Module Compatibility

The primary pathway to enabling Eclipse to function with Java 9 involves editing its configuration file, eclipse.ini. This file dictates runtime parameters for the Eclipse launcher and the OSGi framework it employs.

Approach 1: Explicitly Adding Required Java Modules

One established technique is to instruct the Eclipse launcher to include necessary Java modules that might be missing from the default Java 9 configuration when running the IDE. This is achieved by adding specific arguments to the eclipse.ini file, typically placed after the -vmargs directive.

item.title: Fix JAVA_HOME Not Recognized Error: Step-by-Step Windows Solutions
item.description:
“Fix JAVA_HOME Not Recognized Error: Step-by-Step Windows Solutions”

Encountering the “JAVA_HOME not recognized” error on Windows can halt your Java development workflow. This typically occurs when your system cannot locate the Java Development Kit (JDK) installation. This post delves into various proven methods to correctly configure your environment variables, ensuring your system can find and utilize your JDK.

Locating Your JDK Installation

Before setting any variables, pinpoint the exact installation directory of your JDK. The default location on Windows is often within C:\Program Files\Java.

item.title: Solved: How to fix NullPointerException with @Autowired in Spring Framework
item.description:
“Solved: How to fix NullPointerException with @Autowired in Spring Framework”

At its core, the Spring IoC container acts as a sophisticated manager for your application’s components, often referred to as “beans.” It maintains a registry of these beans (ApplicationContext), configures their properties by injecting dependencies, and orchestrates their creation in the correct order. The crucial point is that the IoC container needs to be aware of an object for it to perform autowiring. If you create an object yourself using the new operator, Spring bypasses its configuration process, leaving any @Autowired fields uninitialized and thus null.
